**What this script does.** It produces the descriptive tables and figures:

| Output file (in `Results/`) | Paper |
|---|---|
| `Table_A1.csv`, `Table_A1.html` | Appendix Table A1 |
| `Fig_1.png` | Figure 1 |
| `Fig_S2.png`, `Fig_S2_data.csv` | Supplementary Figure S2 (change in literacy since Cycle 1) |
| `Fig_S3_B.png`, `Fig_S3_C.png`, `Fig_S3_D.png` | Supplementary Figure S3, panels B–D |
| `Table_S3.csv` | Supplementary Table S3 |
| `Table_S4.csv` | Supplementary Table S4 |
| `Table_UN_migration.csv` | Figures quoted in the introduction |
| `Fig_1_data.csv` | Every number shown in Figure 1 and S3, with standard errors |

**Inputs.** `Data/df2.RDS` from `01_Data_Setup.Rmd`; for Figure S2 also
`Data/piaac_cycle1_lit.rds` from `00_Import.R`.

**Method.** All statistics describe the analysis sample (adults not in
formal education with valid values on every model variable), so that the
descriptives and the models refer to the same people. Means and percentages
use the final weight `SPFWT0`, so pooled results describe the combined adult
population of the countries. Standard errors use the replicate weights with
each country's own replication method, and the ten plausible values are
combined with Rubin's rules. The functions that do this are in
`R/functions_descriptives.R`, which also documents the method.

## Setup

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(here)
source(here("R", "load_packages.R"))
source(here("R", "functions_descriptives.R"))

packages <- c("tidyverse", "here", "knitr", "kableExtra", "ragg", "scales")
load_packages(packages)

dir.create(here("Results"), showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Data and country groups

```{r data}
df2 <- read_rds(here("Data", "df2.RDS"))
dfa <- df2 %>% filter(in_sample == 1)

# Country groups used in Supplementary Figure S3
europe <- c("AUT", "BEL", "CHE", "CZE", "DEU", "DNK", "ESP", "EST", "FIN",
            "FRA", "GBR", "HRV", "HUN", "IRL", "ITA", "LTU", "LVA", "NOR",
            "POL", "PRT", "SVK", "SWE")
rich   <- c("AUT", "BEL", "CHE", "DEU", "DNK", "ESP", "FIN", "FRA", "GBR",
            "IRL", "ITA", "NOR", "PRT", "SWE", "JPN", "CAN", "USA", "NZL")

samples <- list(
  all    = dfa,
  rich   = filter(dfa, iso3c %in% rich),
  europe = filter(dfa, iso3c %in% europe),
  deu    = filter(dfa, iso3c == "DEU"))

tibble(sample = names(samples),
       countries = map_int(samples, ~ n_distinct(.x$iso3c)),
       n = map_int(samples, nrow),
       list = map_chr(samples, ~ paste(sort(unique(.x$iso3c)), collapse = " "))) %>%
  kable()
```

## Table A1. Descriptive statistics

```{r table_a1}
a1_vars <- c(skill_reading = "Literacy (mean of 10 plausible values)",
             NFE12 = "ALE participation",
             female = "Female",
             FORBORN = "Foreign-born",
             FORLANG = "Non-native speaker",
             children = "Has children",
             tertiary = "Tertiary education")

table_a1 <- bind_rows(
  All   = describe_vars(dfa, names(a1_vars), a1_vars),
  Women = describe_vars(filter(dfa, female == 1), names(a1_vars), a1_vars),
  Men   = describe_vars(filter(dfa, female == 0), names(a1_vars), a1_vars),
  .id = "sample") %>%
  filter(!(sample != "All" & variable == "Female"))

write_csv(table_a1, here("Results", "Table_A1.csv"))

table_a1 %>%
  kable(format = "html", digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = "Table A1. Analysis sample, PIAAC Cycle 2. wmean uses the final weight SPFWT0.") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  save_kable(here("Results", "Table_A1.html"))

kable(table_a1, digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Sample flow (also printed in 01):

```{r sample_flow}
tibble(step = c("All respondents (30 countries)",
                "Not currently in formal education",
                "Valid on all model variables"),
       n = c(nrow(df2), sum(df2$ed_currently %in% 0), nrow(dfa))) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Figure 1 and Supplementary Figure S3

Each node of the tree is a group defined by the splits above it: sex, then
birth country, then language, then parenthood. For every node we estimate
mean literacy, the percentage who took part in ALE in the last 12 months and
the percentage with tertiary education, each with its standard error.

```{r tree_stats}
trees <- map(samples, tree_stats)

# One colour scale for all four panels, so equal colours mean equal values
limits <- tree_limits(trees)

bind_rows(trees, .id = "sample") %>%
  select(sample, label, depth, n, mean, se, pct_ale, se_ale,
         pct_tertiary, se_tertiary, pct_below_l2, se_below_l2) %>%
  write_csv(here("Results", "Fig_1_data.csv"))
```

```{r tree_plots}
panels <- tribble(
  ~sample,  ~file,            ~title,
  "all",    "Fig_1.png",      "All Countries",
  "rich",   "Fig_S3_B.png",   "B. High-Income Destination Countries",
  "europe", "Fig_S3_C.png",   "C. Europe",
  "deu",    "Fig_S3_D.png",   "D. Germany")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(panels))) {
  p <- plot_tree(trees[[panels$sample[i]]], panels$title[i], limits)
  agg_png(here("Results", panels$file[i]), res = 200, width = 2000, height = 1000)
  print(p)
  dev.off()
}

include_graphics(here("Results", panels$file))
```

Figure 1 numbers with standard errors (all countries):

```{r tree_table}
trees$all %>%
  select(label, n, mean, se, pct_ale, se_ale, pct_tertiary, se_tertiary) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### German-language versions (not in the paper)

Literacy and numeracy trees for Germany with German labels, for the
GrundbildungsPFADE project. Set `make_german <- FALSE` to skip them.

```{r german}
make_german <- TRUE

if (make_german) {
  de_num <- tree_stats(samples$deu, domain = "NUM")
  german <- list(
    list(stats = trees$deu, domain = "LIT", file = "Fig_S3_D_de_literacy.png",
         title = "Deutschland: Lesekompetenz"),
    list(stats = de_num, domain = "NUM", file = "Fig_S3_D_de_numeracy.png",
         title = "Deutschland: Alltagsmathematik"))
  for (g in german) {
    lim <- tree_limits(list(g$stats))
    agg_png(here("Results", g$file), res = 200, width = 2000, height = 1000)
    print(plot_tree(g$stats, g$title, lim, lang = "de", domain = g$domain))
    dev.off()
  }
  include_graphics(here("Results", map_chr(german, "file")))
}
```

## Supplementary Figure S2. Change in literacy since Cycle 1

Mean literacy in Cycle 2 (2022–23) minus mean literacy in Cycle 1
(2012–17), by country, for all adults and for the foreign-born. This is
the only place PIAAC Cycle 1 is used. Both cycles use all respondents aged
16–65 (not the analysis sample), because the figure frames the paper rather
than describing the model sample. Foreign-born means born outside the
country: `J_Q04a` in Cycle 1, `FORBORN` from 01 in Cycle 2.

Each country mean uses that cycle's final weight, its replicate weights
and the ten plausible values. The two cycles are independent samples, so
the standard error of the change is the square root of the sum of the two
squared standard errors. The countries are those in both cycles.

Caveat: the Cycle 1 plausible values are the ones in the original Cycle 1
public-use files. The OECD's own trend comparisons may use Cycle 1 results
re-estimated on the Cycle 2 scale, which can differ somewhat; check this
before quoting the size of the changes.

```{r fig_s2}
c1_file <- here("Data", "piaac_cycle1_lit.rds")
make_fig_s2 <- file.exists(c1_file)
if (!make_fig_s2) cat("Data/piaac_cycle1_lit.rds not found: run 00_Import.R to make Figure S2.\n")
```

```{r fig_s2_stats, eval = make_fig_s2}
cycles <- list(
  cycle1 = read_rds(c1_file),
  cycle2 = df2 %>% select(iso3c, FORBORN, PVLIT1:PVLIT10, SPFWT0:SPFWT80,
                          VEMETHOD, VEFAYFAC, VENREPS))
both <- intersect(cycles$cycle1$iso3c, cycles$cycle2$iso3c)

# mean literacy (with SE) for one country, cycle and group
cycle_mean <- function(cycle, country, foreign_born_only) {
  d <- filter(cycles[[cycle]], iso3c == country)
  if (foreign_born_only) d <- filter(d, FORBORN %in% 1)
  pv_mean(make_design(d), paste0("PVLIT", 1:10))
}

fig_s2 <- expand_grid(iso3c = both,
                      group = c("All adults", "Foreign-born")) %>%
  mutate(c1 = map2(iso3c, group, ~ cycle_mean("cycle1", .x, .y == "Foreign-born")),
         c2 = map2(iso3c, group, ~ cycle_mean("cycle2", .x, .y == "Foreign-born")),
         mean_cycle1 = map_dbl(c1, "est"), se_cycle1 = map_dbl(c1, "se"),
         mean_cycle2 = map_dbl(c2, "est"), se_cycle2 = map_dbl(c2, "se"),
         change    = mean_cycle2 - mean_cycle1,
         se_change = sqrt(se_cycle1^2 + se_cycle2^2),
         significant = abs(change / se_change) > 1.96) %>%
  select(-c1, -c2)

write_csv(fig_s2, here("Results", "Fig_S2_data.csv"))
kable(fig_s2, digits = 1)
```

How many countries declined (numbers quoted in the paper's framing):

```{r fig_s2_count, eval = make_fig_s2}
fig_s2 %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(countries = n(),
            declined = sum(change < 0),
            declined_significantly = sum(change < 0 & significant),
            rose_significantly = sum(change > 0 & significant)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r fig_s2_plot, eval = make_fig_s2}
country_order <- fig_s2 %>%
  group_by(iso3c) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(change)) %>%
  arrange(m) %>%
  pull(iso3c)

p_s2 <- fig_s2 %>%
  mutate(iso3c = factor(iso3c, levels = country_order)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = iso3c, y = change, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = change - 1.96 * se_change, ymax = change + 1.96 * se_change),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Foreign-born" = "steelblue", "All adults" = "gray70")) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Change in mean literacy (Cycle 2, 2022-23 minus Cycle 1, 2012-17)",
       title = "Change in Mean Literacy between PIAAC Cycles",
       caption = "Weighted means with 95% confidence intervals (replicate weights, 10 plausible values).",
       fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 6, face = "italic"))

agg_png(here("Results", "Fig_S2.png"), res = 144, height = 700, width = 800)
print(p_s2)
dev.off()

include_graphics(here("Results", "Fig_S2.png"))
```

## Supplementary Table S3. The 16 intersectional groups

The bottom row of Figure 1 as a table, with the group's share of the
sample (unweighted) and of the population (weighted).

```{r table_s3}
group_share <- dfa %>%
  group_by(group16) %>%
  summarise(pct_sample = 100 * n() / nrow(dfa),
            pct_population = 100 * sum(SPFWT0) / sum(dfa$SPFWT0))

table_s3 <- trees$all %>%
  filter(depth == 4) %>%
  select(group16 = label, n, mean, se, pct_below_l2, pct_ale, pct_tertiary) %>%
  left_join(group_share, by = "group16") %>%
  relocate(pct_sample, pct_population, .after = n)

write_csv(table_s3, here("Results", "Table_S3.csv"))
kable(table_s3, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Supplementary Table S4. Groups left out of the intersectional figures

Native-born non-native speakers and foreign-born native speakers, by
country: their share of the adult population and their ALE participation
rate. Population is the 2019–2022 average from the Maddison data (in 01).

```{r table_s4}
table_s4 <- dfa %>%
  group_by(iso3c) %>%
  summarise(
    population = first(pop) * 1000,
    pct_native_nonnative = 100 * weighted.mean(FORBORN == 0 & FORLANG == 1, SPFWT0),
    ale_native_nonnative = 100 * weighted.mean(NFE12[FORBORN == 0 & FORLANG == 1],
                                               SPFWT0[FORBORN == 0 & FORLANG == 1]),
    n_native_nonnative   = sum(FORBORN == 0 & FORLANG == 1),
    pct_fb_native        = 100 * weighted.mean(FORBORN == 1 & FORLANG == 0, SPFWT0),
    ale_fb_native        = 100 * weighted.mean(NFE12[FORBORN == 1 & FORLANG == 0],
                                               SPFWT0[FORBORN == 1 & FORLANG == 0]),
    n_fb_native          = sum(FORBORN == 1 & FORLANG == 0))

write_csv(table_s4, here("Results", "Table_S4.csv"))
kable(table_s4, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Migration figures quoted in the introduction

Emigrant numbers and foreign-born population shares by continent, 1990 and
2024. Sources:

- UN DESA (2024), "Total number of emigrants", via Our World in Data,
  <https://ourworldindata.org/migration>.
- UN DESA (2024), "Share of the population that was born in another
  country", via Our World in Data,
  <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/migrant-stock-share>.
- World Bank population 2024 by region (`Data/pop_2024.RDS`, made once by
  `Sub/pop_2024.R`). The World Bank file has no Oceania entry; its 2024
  population is set to 46 million.

The foreign-born share is shown for both "Europe" and "Western Europe (UN)";
the original draft quoted the Western Europe figure as "Europe".

```{r un_migration}
continents <- c("Africa", "Asia", "Europe", "North America", "Oceania",
                "South America")

emigrants <- read_csv(here("Data", "total-number-of-emigrants.filtered",
                           "total-number-of-emigrants.csv")) %>%
  filter(Entity %in% continents, Year %in% c(1990, 2024)) %>%
  select(Entity, Year, emigrants = `Total number of emigrants`) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = emigrants, names_prefix = "emig_")
emigrants <- bind_rows(emigrants,
                       summarise(emigrants, Entity = "World",
                                 across(starts_with("emig_"), sum)))

fb_share <- read_csv(here("Data", "migrant-stock-share.filtered",
                          "migrant-stock-share.csv")) %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(1990, 2024)) %>%
  select(Entity, Year, share = 4) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = share, names_prefix = "pct_fb_")

population <- read_rds(here("Data", "pop_2024.RDS")) %>%
  filter(Entity != "World") %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(Entity = "Oceania", population_2024 = 46e6))
population <- bind_rows(population,
                        tibble(Entity = "World",
                               population_2024 = sum(population$population_2024)))

table_un <- emigrants %>%
  full_join(fb_share, by = "Entity") %>%
  filter(Entity != "Japan") %>%
  left_join(population, by = "Entity") %>%
  transmute(Entity,
            emigrants_2024 = emig_2024,
            pct_change_emigrants_1990_2024 = 100 * (emig_2024 - emig_1990) / emig_1990,
            pct_emigrants_2024 = 100 * emig_2024 / population_2024,
            pct_fb_1990, pct_fb_2024)

write_csv(table_un, here("Results", "Table_UN_migration.csv"))
kable(table_un, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```
